_note: Modern English → KJV vocabulary, for PARAPHRASE SEARCH ONLY.
Why this exists: the bundled text is 1611 English, but a preacher retelling a
story speaks 2026 English. Measured on data/paraphrase_corpus.json, a natural
retelling ('the paralysed man lowered through the roof') found the right
passage 18% of the time, because not one of its content words appears in the
KJV at all. That is a VOCABULARY gap, not a semantics gap — and a vocabulary
gap is a table, not a neural network.
Applied to the QUERY ONLY, never to the index. Expanding the corpus would
corrupt the IDF weights that make rare biblical nouns such strong signals.
Deliberately GENERAL KJV archaisms, not a list reverse-engineered from the
failing cases — otherwise the benchmark would just be measuring itself. Terms
unique to one story (a 'Samaritan', a 'sycomore') are left out on purpose: a
gloss that names an answer is not a gloss, it is a cheat.
This is the same shape as data/book_aliases.json: hand-curated, offline, and
reviewable by anyone who knows the text. It does NOT replace a sentence
embedder — it closes the cheap half of the gap first.
